entries.text: Before diving into Corbin's cosmology, Voss establishes a crucial distinction between two modes of knowing. One is Aristotelian: rational, analytical, the observer separate from the observed. The other is Platonic: participatory, intuitive, the knower united with the known. Corbin's entire project sits firmly in the second camp.

entries.text: In this cosmology, the imagination is not a human faculty projecting fantasies. It is the angelic mode of perception. Angels do not have physical senses, so they perceive through imagination. When humans cultivate the active imagination, they are literally learning to perceive as angels perceive.

entries.text: The Burning Bush is the paradigmatic example because it makes the principle concrete. The same phenomenon presents itself differently depending on the faculty brought to it: to the senses, a brushwood fire; to the imagination operating at full capacity, a theophany. The difference is in the perceiver.

entries.text: Corbin's alchemy has nothing to do with gold. Forget the furnace. What he's describing is a soul learning to see through itself — spirit and matter meeting at a seam most people never notice is there.
